subject: URGENT: LatticeCore AZ2 throughput & 5xx spike — cross-region reroute request
messages:
From: Jane Ortiz <jane.ortiz@latticecore.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Support Ops <supportops@latticecore.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2027 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Production latency + 5xx spike — US-WEST2 AZ2

Hi Laura,

We're seeing a severe drop in throughput and a sustained 5xx spike in US-WEST2 AZ2 starting ~07:45 PST. Error rate jumped from ~0.4% to ~12% and median latency climbed from 120ms to 2.2s. Our clients are timing out — we already have three high-touch customers flagged.

Attached is a short excerpt from our request logs (request_log_excerpt.txt). Key points:
- Spike aligns with a flurry of longer-context requests to the same model family.
- KV cache hit-rates dropped significantly for AZ2 only.
- We can reproduce higher latencies from our end hitting the AZ2 endpoints.

This needs immediate attention. Can Redwood perform a cross-region reroute to US-WEST3 (or fallback cluster) while your team investigates AZ2? We need an ETA and confirmation that session affinity and keys will be preserved or gracefully degraded. Also please advise whether this qualifies for an incident credit or support escalations.

Jane Ortiz
Head of Platform Reliability, LatticeCore
Jane Ortiz | jane.ortiz@latticecore.com | +1 (415) 555-0134

--

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2027 09:05:21 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Production latency + 5xx spike — US-WEST2 AZ2

Team — forwarding urgent report from LatticeCore (attached excerpt). Impact: enterprise customer, multiple timed-out requests, potential downstream SLA hits.

Please confirm the following ASAP:
1) Can we perform a controlled traffic drift for LatticeCore from us-west2 AZ2 -> us-west3 (or nearest compatible cluster) and preserve session affinity for active conversations?
2) Ops steps & ETA for the reroute; expected client-visible disruption window.
3) Whether we can warm caches / pre-populate KV for the canary target to reduce cold-start amplification.
4) Ask Rishi: one-time remedial credit authority and messaging for the customer.

I am copying Diego for routing execution and Hannah for playbook. If we need exec-level sign-off for credits or capacity, I'll escalate. I will also keep Jane and their Support Ops in the loop.

Laura
Laura Bennett | Director, Customer Engineering | Redwood Inference

--Forwarded message follows--
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2027 10:00:05 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production latency + 5xx spike — US-WEST2 AZ2

Laura / Diego — quick ops plan below. I will start the runbook immediately and request the routing change once we validate the target capacity.

Immediate steps (0-30m):
- Identify all active routes for LatticeCore (in routing service). Confirm model compatibility in us-west3. (Diego)
- Launch controlled canary: shift 5% traffic to us-west3 for 10m, monitor errors/latency and KV cache hit ratio. (Diego)
- If canary stable, ramp to 50% over next 15m with automated rollback on >3% additional error rate.
- Before ramp, pre-warm KV: replay recent prefixes for top 10 customer sessions to target cluster (cache-warm job). This should reduce cold misses.

Risk notes:
- Some sessions tied to AZ2 local storage may see degraded contextual continuity if we can't warm every KV. We'll surface any dropped contexts to the customer.
- We must ensure any model variant fallback used in us-west3 is functionally compatible (tokenization, max-length).

Evidence: network_diagnostics.zip contains traceroutes and connection timing showing AZ2 egress jitter.

Request to Rishi (Cc'd): please approve the go-ahead for the routing change and confirm whether we should include a one-time remediation credit in the communication. I recommend offering a 20% credit on affected billing for the period until full remediation (~48h window) to prioritize customer satisfaction.

I'll open JIRA INF-11234 and populate runbook steps. Diego — coordinate with infra to reserve burst capacity if needed.

Hannah
Hannah Schmitt | Sr. Manager, Reliability Engineering | Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2027 11:30:41 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production latency + 5xx spike — US-WEST2 AZ2

Thanks — I approve the controlled cross-region drift as described.

On the commercial side I authorize a one-time remedial credit up to 20% for impacted usage for the initial 48-hour window pending a post-incident review. Please capture the affected timeframe and metric thresholds in the customer comms. I want CS to draft the note with an empathetic tone and clear next steps; cc me on the outgoing message.

Also: if we need dedicated burst capacity in us-west3 to absorb traffic, route the procurement/infra request through Chad (capacity team) and tag the ticket as P0. We'll absorb incremental cost for a short period.

Rishi
Rishi Malhotra | VP, Sales & Customer Success | Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jane Ortiz <jane.ortiz@latticecore.com>, Support Ops <supportops@latticecore.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2027 15:45:12 -0800
Subject: Re: Production latency + 5xx spike — US-WEST2 AZ2 (actioning reroute)

Jane / LatticeCore —

Thank you for the details and patience. Quick update and actions we've taken: 

1) We initiated a controlled cross-region reroute at 15:10 PST from US-WEST2 AZ2 to US-WEST3 (5% -> 50% over 30m ramp) and observed error-rate regression to baseline within the canary window.
2) We pre-warmed KV cache for the top session prefixes; most active sessions show restored latency (~130-160ms). A small subset of long-history sessions may see missing context; we'll list these in the post-incident notes.
3) Our runbook is tracked in JIRA INF-11234 (link below). Diego is monitoring the ramp and will perform a full cut if stability holds.
4) Commercial: Rishi approved a one-time remedial credit of up to 20% for the affected 48-hour window. We'll have CS send the formal credit confirmation today.

Attachments: reroute_timeline.csv (timeline + rollback thresholds). We also uploaded network diagnostics to the shared drive.

Next steps:
- Diego / Hannah: continue monitoring for 4 hours and hold on full bridge-back until we have remediation root cause.
- Redwood to provide post-incident report within 72 hours including root cause analysis and mitigations.
- CS will reach out with formal credit details.

Jane, apologies for the disruption. We're treating this as a P0 and I'll keep you updated at the 30m cadence until we resolve.

Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Engineering | Redwood Inference
